doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Repertory bands: Mingus, Ellington, Roach-Brown, Blakey, Silver
summary: He names bands whose repertories are essential models, including Max Roach and Clifford Brown, Parker and Gillespie, Horace Silver and Art Blakey's Messengers.

blocks.x: Are you speaking of people like Charles Mingus and Ellington?

Oh absolutely. Absolutely. But also Max Roach and Clifford Brown. They created a repertory that will live forever, a repertory of using the Great American Songbook, as well as their own compositions, and putting arrangements to them that will last forever. I mean the show — Broadway writers had no idea that those beautiful songs that they wrote that became a part of the American Songbook could be completely made even better you know, with chord substitutions and rhythmical arrangements and rhythmical

displacement, and you know the American Songbook, if you are not a composer you don’t need it because it’s just so much to work with there, you know, that you can make arrangements out of. But I mean Mingus, I mean with the small group Mingus and, well, Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie, that model is still king as far as I’m concerned. If you’re getting this, yes we have all this that’s going on now, with these different types of musical theatrical events. But if you’re not dealing with that model in some fashion, okay, it might be great music but it’s not in this particular part of the art form. So yeah, Max Roach and Clifford Brown, that’s a book, a repertory book all by itself. At least two or three Miles Davis’ repertory bands, Horace Silver — you could spend your entire lifetime using that repertory or that style, Art Blakey the same thing. The great thing about Art Blakey as opposed to Horace Silver who was a pianist so he wrote all his material which is now our American Songbook basically. Jazz music songbook. But Art Blakey, he drew or put in his band, you know, on each instrument just incredible musicians who were great composers. So that’s a whole repertory by itself you know, indispensable. Like Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie is indispensible, that model. Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers, especially the ones from the beginning through 1965, that’s totally indispensable if you’re going to be in this and have the validity. You have to know that material. And so, yeah.
